sentences.text: Kirthi Balaraju, vs The District Collector, Karimnagar ... on 6

Author: T. Vinod Kumar
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition No.11451 of 2015
Order:

Heard learned counsel for petitioners, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and Sri P.Sri Harsha Reddy, learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.4, and perused the record.

2. Shorn of unnecessary details, the case of the petitioners in brief is that though the respondent authorities have passed consent award on 24-12-2012, the petitioners aggrieved by the compensation determined thereunder had approached the respondent authorities and submitted application dated 15-01-2013 (filed on 28-01-2013) seeking reference to Court under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act') for determination of the market value of the structure, and in spite of petitioners submitting the aforesaid application, the same has not been considered, which action on the part of the respondent authorities, it is contended as illegal and arbitrary.

3. Per contra, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondents on the other hand submits that the award passed is a consent award in respect of land to an extent of Ac.294.3 gts situated at Ladnapur village, Peddapalli District; that the petitioners have also expressed their willingness to receive compensation under consent award by executing an affidavit in Form-IV; and that the authorities on the basis of the consent award have also made payment to the petitioners.

4. Learned Government Pleader and learned Standing Counsel further submit that the petitioners after receiving the compensation amount under consent award, as an after thought, have approached the respondent authorities and submitted application under Section 18 of the Act seeking reference, which course of action is not permitted, in view of the fact that petitioners themselves having agreed for compensation amount, have indicated their consent in writing for passing of consent award.
5. I have taken note of respective contentions urged.

6. A reading of the award shows that the petitioners have agreed for settlement of compensation under Negotiations Rules, 1992 r/w Section 11(2) of the Act, and the respondent authorities accordingly paid compensation thereunder.

It is also an admitted fact that the petitioners have Kirthi Balaraju, vs The District Collector, Karimnagar ... on 6 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135700793/
1 agreed to receive the compensation under consent award by taking part in the negotiations meeting held, whereby the payment of compensation has been finalized as package deal under the A.P. Land Acquisition (Negotiations Committee) Rules, 1992, subject to condition that the land owners shall not agitate for enhanced compensation in any Court of law under Section 18 of the Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. As the petitioners have agreed to receive the compensation as package deal under the said Rules,
more particularly having also filed an affidavit in Form-IV with the concerned authorities on 02-05-2013, it is not open for the petitioners thereafter to turn around to approach the respondent authorities and submit application under Section 18 of the Act seeking reference to Court claiming that they are only sanctioned compensation in respect of land and not in respect of the structures.

It is to be noted that there cannot be any piece-meal adjudication of land acquisition proceedings consisting of land and structure thereon and thus, the claim of the petitioners of the respondent authorities not making reference to Court by considering their application submitted on 28-01-2013, in the considered view of this Court, is devoid of merit and has to fail.
8.
Accordingly, the Writ Petition is dismissed.
9. As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending if any shall stand closed.
